Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines (Liability cap and refunds)

Monica,

Thanks for the call this morning — attaching our redlines to the MSA and the Order Form. Two short items we want to confirm before we proceed to procurement:

1) Limitation of Liability: we redlined a $5M cap and asked that consequential damages be excluded.
2) Termination / refunds: we proposed a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for termination for convenience and a requirement for 30 days wind-down assistance.

We flagged the interplay between the LoL cap and the termination/refund language — our counsel prefers that refunds (which can be material for large prepaids) be carved out from the cap so that Acme can recover prepaid amounts above the cap in a narrow set of circumstances. Please let us know Redwood's position.

Subject: internal: Acme MSA redline — LoL v refund carve-outs (analysis)

Team,

Quick read of Acme's redlines and the ask to carve refunds out of the LoL cap. Key points and suggested positions below.

Summary of the risk: Acme's position would allow prepaid refunds to be claimed in full even if the LoL cap is lower — for large prepaids that could exceed our intended exposure.

Suggested position (balanced):
- Maintain an overall LoL cap tied to the greater of (i) fees paid in the prior 12 months, or (ii) $1,000,000. This aligns with our standard and is defensible.
- Exclude from the cap direct refunds of prepaid, unused fees where termination for convenience is exercised, but only up to the amount of unused prepaid fees less documented wind-down costs and non-refundable third-party charges.
- Specifically preserve carve-outs for damages resulting from gross negligence, willful misconduct, and breaches of confidentiality or data protection (standard exceptions).
- For consequential damages: continue to exclude them, but allow recovery of direct refunds and costs (not consequential or speculative business loss).

Draft compromise clause we can propose to Acme (high-level language for negotiation):
"Notwithstanding the limitation of liability set forth above, Customer shall be entitled to the refund of any prepaid, unused fees paid under an Order Form upon termination for convenience, provided that such refund shall be net of reasonable documented wind-down assistance costs and any non-refundable third-party expenses; such refunds shall constitute direct damages and shall not be treated as consequential damages for the purposes of this Agreement. This refund remedy shall be subject to the overall limitation of liability, except that the parties agree that recovery of prepaid, unused fees under this Section shall not increase Company’s liability beyond the greater of (a) fees paid in the prior 12 months, or (b) $1,000,000."

That last sentence is intentionally narrow — it preserves a cap while allowing refunds up to the cap. If Acme insists on an unconditional carve-out (refunds unlimited), we should push back hard; operationally we can also propose an escrow or letter of credit for very large prepaids.

Happy to join a call with Acme's counsel — recommend Monica run commercial tradeoffs (wind-down days, cost categories) on the call.

Vivek
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (Liability cap and refunds)

Team — thanks for the quick internal review, Vivek. A few comments from Acme counsel:

- Acme will not accept a cap that effectively limits recovery of prepaid fees where the refund is unrelated to breach (i.e., termination for convenience). They want refunds to be outside the cap.
- Acme is open to a netting approach for wind-down costs (i.e., refunds less documented costs), but will push to keep wind-down deductions narrowly defined.
- If Redwood insists on an overall cap that includes refunds, Acme asks for an exception for (i) refunds of prepaid fees and (ii) amounts paid to third parties for termination assistance up to a reasonable threshold.

Proposed next step: redline the specific paragraph in the MSA we discussed, and include an illustrative refund calculation for the Order Form (example: $2.4M prepaid, 30 days unused = $1.2M refund before wind-down deductions). That will help negotiators converge.

-Kyle
Senior Counsel
Mills & Co. (outside counsel for Acme)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme.com>, Kyle Mills <kyle.mills@millsco.com>

Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (Liability cap and refunds) — Redwood proposal

Elena / Kyle — appreciate the candid feedback and the example; helpful. Per our internal discussion, Redwood can agree to a narrowly tailored refund carve-out coupled with protections so our commercial exposure remains bounded. Main points we propose for the revised MSA / Order Form:

1) Liability Cap: remain the greater of (a) fees paid in prior 12 months, or (b) $1,000,000 (this is our standard).
2) Refund carve-out: Customer may receive refund of prepaid, unused fees upon termination for convenience, net of documented wind-down assistance costs and any non-refundable third-party charges. Refunds will be treated as direct damages and not consequential damages.
3) Interaction with Cap: refunds of prepaid, unused fees will be recoverable up to the LoL cap (i.e., they will not create additional liability beyond the cap).
4) Exceptions: carve-outs for willful misconduct, gross negligence, and breaches of data protection/confidentiality remain unlimited as set forth in Section [X].
4) Commercial safeguard: for prepaids exceeding $2M, Redwood requests either (a) an escrow or letter of credit for the prepaid amount, or (b) a negotiated higher cap for that Order Form.

Next steps — see attached proposed redline that implements the above and an illustrative refund calculation (OrderForm-Acme-v2.docx). If that reads cleanly for Acme, we can schedule a 30-minute call Thursday to finalize. If Acme cannot accept the cap interaction, please surface the specific commercial consequences so we can evaluate alternate mitigations (escrow/LOC, higher per-Order Form cap, or agreed wind-down fee schedule).

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
